extracted.intended_audience: Newbery selection committee members, librarians, children's authors, and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Official terms, definitions, eligibility rules, and literary quality criteria used to determine the Newbery Medal and Honor books (most distinguished contribution to American literature for children published in the U.S. in English during the preceding year). Includes granular evaluation dimensions (theme, plot, character, style, etc.) and procedural eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal award scope and basic eligibility (Term 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal shall be awarded annually to the author of the most distinguished contribution to American literature for children published by an American publisher in the United States in English during the preceding year. There are no limitations as to the character of the book considered except that it be original work. Honor books may be named. These shall be books that are also truly distinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the overall purpose: annual award to the single most distinguished text for children; allows honor books; requires originality and U.S. publication in English by an American publisher in the preceding year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author nationality/residency restriction (Term 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Award is restricted to authors who are citizens or residents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only U.S. citizens or residents are eligible as authors (authors may be co-authors; posthumous awards allowed per definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee must consider only eligible books (Term 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee in its deliberations is to consider only the books eligible for the award, as specified in the terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection should be confined to works meeting the stated eligibility rules (publication date, language, publisher, residency, originality, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — contribution to American literature (Definition 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Contribution to American literature” indicates the text of a book. It also implies that the committee shall consider all forms of writing—fiction, non-fiction, and poetry. Reprints, compilations and abridgements are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the primacy of the text and that any literary form is acceptable; excludes reprints, compilations, and abridgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — contribution to American literature for children (Definition 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A “contribution to American literature for children” shall be a book for which children are an intended potential audience. The book displays respect for children’s understandings, abilities, and appreciations. Children are defined as persons of ages up to and including fourteen, and books for this entire age range are to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility depends on intended audience (children up to 14) and respect for children's capacities; includes books across the full childhood age range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'Distinguished' (Definition 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Distinguished” is defined as: • Marked by eminence and distinction; noted for significant achievement. • Marked by excellence in quality. • Marked by conspicuous excellence or eminence. • Individually distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides multi-faceted meaning of 'distinguished' emphasizing outstanding quality, significance, and individuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'Author' (Definition 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Author” may include co-authors. The author(s) may be awarded the medal posthumously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that multiple authors are eligible and posthumous awards are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'Original work' (Definition 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'original work' means that the text was created by this writer and no one else. It may include original retellings of traditional literature, provided the words are the author’s own. Further, 'original work' means that the text is presented here for the first time and has not been previously published elsewhere in this or any other form. Text reprinted or compiled from other sources are not eligible. Abridgements are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality covers both authorship and first publication; retellings allowed only if words are the author's; excludes previously published text, reprints, compilations, and abridgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'In English' (Definition 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: “In English” means that the committee considers only books written and published in English. This requirement DOES NOT limit the use of words or phrases in another language where appropriate in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary language must be English, but the appropriate inclusion of other-language words/phrases is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'American literature published in the United States' (Definition 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: “American literature published in the United States” means that books first published in previous years in other countries are not eligible. Books published simultaneously in the U.S. and another country may be eligible. Books published in a U.S. territory, or U.S. commonwealth are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disqualifies works first published abroad in prior years; allows simultaneous international publication and publication in U.S. territories/commonwealths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'Published…in the preceding year' (Definition 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Published…in the preceding year” means that the book has a publication date in that year, was available for purchase in that year, and has a copyright date no later than that year. A book might have a copyright date prior to the year under consideration but, for various reasons, was not published until the year under consideration. If a book is published prior to its year of copyright as stated in the book, it shall be considered in its year of copyright as stated in the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies eligibility by publication/copyright date so each book is considered in only one year; intent is to ensure availability and avoid multi-year consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'Resident' (Definition 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Resident” specifies that the author has established and maintains a residence in the United States, U.S. territory, or U.S. commonwealth as distinct from being a casual or occasional visitor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency means established/maintained residence, not casual or occasional presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'Only the books eligible for the award' (Definition 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term, “only the books eligible for the award,” specifies that the committee is not to consider the entire body of the work by an author or whether the author has previously won the award. The committee’s decision is to be made following deliberation about the books of the specified calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee must evaluate each candidate book on its own merits for the eligibility year, ignoring author’s past wins or other works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of the theme or concept (Criteria 1a — element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation of the theme or concept
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the literary qualities committee members should consider; strength judged by how effectively the theme/concept is explored for the intended child audience. Note: Because literary qualities vary by content, excellence is not required in every element, but the book should have distinguished qualities in the elements pertinent to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of information — accuracy, clarity, organization (Criteria 1a — element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of information including accuracy, clarity, and organization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate factual accuracy (for nonfiction), clarity of exposition, and organizational effectiveness for children; again, excellence may vary by book type but pertinent elements should be distinguished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of plot (Criteria 1a — element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of a plot
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the plotting appropriate to the work's form and intended age range — pacing, structure, coherence, and narrative satisfaction for child readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delineation of characters (Criteria 1a — element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Delineation of characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge characterization depth, distinctiveness, and appropriateness for children’s understanding and appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delineation of setting (Criteria 1a — element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Delineation of a setting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how setting is rendered and how it supports theme, plot, and child reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of style (Criteria 1a — element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider voice, diction, and stylistic choices that suit the intended child audience and the book's goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of presentation for a child audience (Criteria 1b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members must consider excellence of presentation for a child audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation quality should be judged with child readers in mind — readability, engagement, and respect for children's abilities and understandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary basis — the text (Criteria 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each book is to be considered as a contribution to American literature. The committee is to make its decision primarily on the text. Other components of a book, such as illustrations, overall design of the book, etc., may be considered when they make the book less effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual literary quality is the central basis for the award; paratextual elements (illustrations, design) are secondary and only factored when they detract from effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained entity requirement (Criteria 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media (i.e., sound or film equipment) for its enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that require external media or equipment for enjoyment are ineligible; the book must stand alone as a literary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award focus — literary quality, not didactic content or popularity (Note)
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee should keep in mind that the award is for literary quality and quality presentation for children. The award is not for didactic content or popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection should prioritize artistic and literary merit and presentation appropriate for children over instructional/manual value or commercial/popular success.
